items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025

ctx.x: Yeah I think the trumpet has that ability more so than other instruments. You know I taught in the public schools for about 12, 13 years and I taught woodwind and brass. I taught clarinet, you know, tenor, alto, trombone, I had some trumpet students. And yeah it’s like the trumpet has a certain magnetism that attracts certain types of people, you know really loud outspoken people or maybe really reserved people that want to have something that’s on the opposite end of what they are. And then you have some that…

brass, Maynard Ferguson style. And then you have other people, it’s like I really want to make this brass instrument that wants to be loud and high be something that’s more subtle like Chet Baker or, you know somebody else. So yeah for me it’s probably a mix of that. But I say I’ve really gotten a little bit out of my — I mean I’ve gotten older and, you know, developed more as a person and so I’ve kind of come out of my shell that way but I think just being on the educational side of things really opened me up…

I think you’re right. And among the things I’ve done, one of the toughest was learning how to deal with like kindergarten and first grade classes. You know if you can figure that out, that makes a lot of other things just seem easy.
